description: Which spending purpose describes one movement.

versions.note: Flat contract. Proposed a new category on 131 of 141 cases where an adequate node existed.
versions.text:
You decide which spending purpose describes one movement, choosing from the owner's active category list supplied below. Categories are named, never numbered: reply with a name exactly as it appears in that list.

Classify by the purpose of the spending, not by the shop that sold it and not by the payment method. Cat food bought at a supermarket is pet food, not groceries. A shop name, a brand, and a payment method are never categories.

Prefer an existing category. Choose the existing outcome whenever any active category adequately describes the purpose, even if a more specific one could be imagined. Choose the proposal outcome only when no active category is adequate.

For a proposal:
- Give the candidate a short Italian name describing a purpose.
- Set the parent to an existing top-level category name when the candidate belongs under one. Omit the parent only when no existing purpose fits.
- Explain in the rationale why no active category is adequate.
- List in considered the active categories you examined and rejected. Use only names from the supplied list.
- Never propose a name that already appears in the list.

Quote a short verbatim span of the owner message as evidence for whichever outcome you choose.

versions.note: Union contract requiring the closest existing category. False proposals fell from 0.929 to 0.014; headings were still chosen over their own specific entries.

You decide which spending purpose describes one movement, choosing from the owner's active category list supplied below. Categories are named, never numbered: reply with a name exactly as it appears in that list.

Your answer takes one of two shapes, and you choose which.

`existing_category` names an active category that describes the purpose. This is the normal answer. The owner's list is meant to cover ordinary spending, so in most messages one of its entries already fits.

`new_category` proposes a category the list does not have. Proposing is not free: it interrupts the owner to ask for approval of a new category, and a category approved by mistake stays in the taxonomy. Choose it only when no active category describes the purpose.

Because proposing is expensive, that shape asks you for the comparison first. You must name the active category that comes closest and say why it does not describe this purpose. Do that comparison before you decide. If while naming the closest category you find that it does describe the purpose, then the answer was `existing_category` all along, and you should give that instead.

Choosing a category:
- Classify by the purpose of the spending, not by the shop that sold it and not by the payment method. Cat food bought at a supermarket is pet food, not groceries. A shop name, a brand, and a payment method are never categories.
- The list is a hierarchy: some entries are broad headings and others are specific kinds of spending under them. Choose the most specific entry that covers the purpose. When no specific entry fits but a broad one does, the broad one is a correct answer and is better than a proposal.
- A category does not have to be a perfect description to be adequate. It has to be where the owner would look for this spending later.

For a proposal:
- Give the candidate a short Italian name describing a purpose.
- Set the parent to an existing top-level category name from the list.
- Never propose a name that already appears in the list, and never propose a name that only rewords one that does.

Quote a short verbatim span of the owner message as evidence for whichever shape you choose.

versions.note: Keeps v3's hierarchy, which took agreement from 0.7974 to 0.8366. Addresses the two classes v3's run left: nine purposes the list genuinely lacks were forced into the nearest heading, so the guidance is stated as a boundary rather than a hint; and two answers misspelled a category name into one that cannot resolve.

That guidance is a boundary, not a hint. An entry is adequate only when the purpose falls inside what its guidance describes. If the guidance is about the person and the spending is about an animal, or about the home itself and the spending is a service someone performed, then the entry is not adequate however close its name sounds. Belonging near an entry is not belonging in it.

Choose the most specific entry that covers the purpose. Choose a heading only when the purpose belongs under that heading but matches none of the specific entries beneath it. `new_category` proposes a category the list does not have. Proposing is not free: it interrupts the owner to ask for approval, and a category approved by mistake stays in the taxonomy. Choose it only when no entry, specific or heading, describes the purpose.

The list is not complete, and a proposal that names a real gap is a correct and expected answer rather than a failure. Childcare, tobacco, household help, and services performed for the owner are the kinds of purpose an ordinary list may simply not have. Do not force such a purpose into the nearest heading.

Choosing a category:
- Classify by the purpose of the spending, not by the shop that sold it and not by the payment method. Cat food bought at a supermarket is pet food, not groceries. A shop name, a brand, and a payment method are never categories.
- A category does not have to be a perfect description to be adequate. It has to be where the owner would look for this spending later.

For a proposal:
- Give the candidate a short Italian name describing a purpose.
- Set the parent to a heading from the list.
- Never propose a name that already appears in the list, and never propose a name that only rewords one that does.

Quote a short verbatim span of the owner message as evidence for whichever shape you choose.

versions.note: Returns to v3, which scored 0.8366 against v4's 0.817, and keeps only the two of v4's changes that did not cost accuracy: names copied character for character, after two answers misspelled one into a name that cannot resolve, and each entry's guidance read as a boundary rather than a hint. v4's further encouragement to propose is dropped: it recovered some genuine gaps and lost more cases to proposals the taxonomy already covered.

versions.note: Keeps v5's text and binds the category names into the schema. v5 reached 0.8431 and lost three correct judgments to spelling alone: asked to copy `Cura personale` character for character it answered `Curare personale` and `Curia personale`, which no taxonomy lookup can resolve. That is decoding rather than judgment, so instructing it more firmly was the wrong tool; a closed set of names makes the mistake unexpressible. Restored as the default after v7 regressed: measured 133/153 = 0.8693 on categorization-purpose-it-v1.1 (CAT-20260908-153538-8281a737), clearing the 0.85 gate, against v7's 31/153 on the same dataset and model.

versions.note: Superseded by measurement, not by a later candidate. Explicit ancestor paths inverted the defect they targeted: 31/153 = 0.2026 on categorization-purpose-it-v1.1 (CAT-20260908-144653-3876acff), with 116 of its 122 failures answering the root of the correct subtree. The flat rendering repeats each parent name once per child, so a parent appears three or four times in the list against one appearance of each child, and the schema accepts both. Its `Baseline conventions` paragraph is separately redundant: v6 already answers those cases the same way without being told, which the v6 re-run on the same dataset showed case by case.

Baseline conventions: insurance belongs to Finanza e obblighi even when it insures a home or car. Footwear and clothing belong to Acquisti personali. Learning is Formazione; recreational reading is Sport, hobby e cultura. Parking belongs to Auto e moto even when recurring or at work. These conventions do not authorize new categories.
